Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo last week — good discussion. Attached are our redlines to the MSA and the Order Form. Key asks from Aurelia Legal/Procurement:

- Output ownership: we need a clear assignment of ‘‘Customer product output’’ generated by the service so our product team can ship features that include model responses.
- Training/data use: we cannot grant rights for Redwood to use customer content or outputs to train models without explicit opt-in. Proposed language: no training on Customer Content or Outputs for any purpose unless Customer signs a separate training consent amendment.
- Feedback license: we expect standard feedback protections limited to bug fixes and non-derivative improvements, and only if aggregated and anonymized.

These are blocking items for procurement — we can be flexible on time-limited telemetry and aggregated telemetry for operational improvement, but not on training.

Attached: Aurelia_MSA_redline_20271006.docx and OrderForm_Aurelia_v3.pdf

Subject: Re: Fwd: Aurelia redlines (MSA + Order Form) - IP and training

Kimberly — draft summary and recommended positions below. Uploaded a tracked-change redline to the Drive link (see thread links).

1) Output ownership (proposed Redwood position)
- Offer: exclusive-ish operational right for the Customer to use, reproduce, and commercialize Outputs as part of Customer products, subject to: (a) exclusions for Redwood-delivered model internals and (b) no assignment of underlying model weights or productized model code.
- Compromise language: "Customer shall have sole ownership of Customer Output as delivered by the Service for use in Customer's products and services; Redwood retains ownership of the Service, models, model weights, and any derivative internal training artifacts."

2) Training / data use (proposed Redwood position)
- Reject blanket prohibition. Offer: no training on Customer Content or Outputs for general model improvement without explicit written opt-in. Provide limited, time-bound operational telemetry exception: Redwood may use aggregated/anonymous telemetry and data for debugging, security, and performance tuning.
- Option: 90-day opt-out window (Customer can elect to opt-out of any training within 90 days post-delivery) OR a 12-month embargo for non-consented training. Recommend 90 days as more sale-friendly.

3) Feedback license (proposed Redwood position)
- Narrow feedback license: Customer grants Redwood a non-exclusive, worldwide, royalty-free license to use Feedback provided by Customer to improve the Service, provided such Feedback is aggregated and pseudonymized. No rights to derive or assign Customer Output.

4) Non-negotiables for Sales to present
- Redwood retains ownership of models, weights, and production improvements.
- Any training use requires explicit written consent.
- Telemetry carveout for safety/debugging must be preserved.

I'll prepare a tracked redline MSA and a short memo for Sales to send to Aurelia procurement. If Rishi or Kimberly want stricter language (e.g., 12-month embargo), flag now — we'll include fallback positions.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

James / Maya — thanks for the detailed redlines. Laura (Redwood Legal) and I reviewed and propose the following compromise positions to move toward signature without further delay: 

1) Customer Output: Redwood will accept language confirming Customer's right to use, reproduce, and commercialize Outputs generated by the Service for Customer products. We cannot assign ownership of Redwood's models, model weights, or internal tooling. Proposed sentence: "Customer shall have ownership and full rights with respect to Outputs created by the Service for Customer's use; nothing in this Agreement transfers ownership of Redwood's models, weights, or Service infrastructure to Customer."

2) Training / data use: Redwood will agree that Customer Content and Customer Outputs will not be used to train Redwood's general-purpose models for production improvement absent a separate written consent. As a saleable compromise, Redwood requests the right to use aggregated and anonymized telemetry for safety, debugging, and performance tuning. We propose a 90-day embargo after delivery during which Customer may opt in or opt out of training use by executing the standard training consent amendment. If reasonable to your procurement timeline, we can add explicit Order Form checkbox language for training consent.

3) Feedback: we will accept a narrow feedback license limited to aggregated/pseudonymized usage and internal improvements (no assignment).

Next steps: Laura will send a tracked-change redline to your team today reflecting this language; if Aurelia procurement is comfortable, we can add a one-line training consent checkbox on the Order Form so signature can proceed without a separate amendment.

If you need a quicker exec-level approval, I'm available for a 20-minute call this afternoon to finalize language.

Best,
